clue.text: He stirs up the mob dreadfully, bar our rebels

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the words bar our rebels are badly mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demagogue whips up a crowd with a terrible slogan about rebels and a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' looks like it qualifies the stirring, but it signals rearranging BAR OUR REBELS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser is an agitator who incites a crowd to unrest.

clue.text: Comeback of one with job in engineering group

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation for the engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
I is the Roman numeral one
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Someone working for an engineering firm answers back.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, a verbal return.

clue.text: One producing ring, say, for a beautiful woman

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: a bell is something that rings

explanation.surface: Someone offers a ring to a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing ring' suggests a jeweller or a proposal, but it is something that makes a ringing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a woman admired for her looks, the beauty of the ball.

clue.text: Have Latin translated — it means "sea monster"

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry claiming a Latin word means a sea beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' looks like a language instruction but signals rearranging HAVE LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a giant biblical sea creature.

clue.text: Not quite the way to turn up

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a route is the way to go

explanation.surface: Directions that don't quite tell you how to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like 'arrive' but means dig up, as a pig roots with its snout.
explanation.definitionFit: To rout is to root or dig up the ground, as with a snout.

clue.text: Last man admitted by university after the usual time

indicators.note: admitted by means let in, so the name goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: late means after the expected time
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: The final student is let into college after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final or last in a series.

clue.text: Slippery youngster gives new order to characters opening bar

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put into a fresh sequence

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise things open

explanation.surface: A wily child rearranges the letters at the start of a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening bar' looks like the start of a bar but is a bar for opening, a LEVER, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a famously slippery creature.

clue.text: Seeing eye to eye about soldiers getting older

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for getting older wraps round the soldiers

parts.note: ageing means growing older
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Ageing troops find they see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing means sharing the same opinion.

clue.text: Worsted worn by use?

definitions.meaning: trodden down by frequent use, as a path

explanation.definitionFit: Worsted means defeated, and a well-trodden track is worn down by use.

clue.text: One may rise to great heights, in the event

definitions.text: One may rise to great heights, in the event

parts.words: One may rise to great heights, in the event
parts.note: read as an athletics field event in which competitors clear a high bar using a long flexible pole

explanation.surface: A hopeful remark about someone's future success, if things go well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the event' reads as 'as it turns out', but means a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: This athletics discipline sends competitors soaring over a bar several metres up.

clue.text: Very bad fever? It's not clear

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Someone's high temperature leaves them muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is hazy or imprecise, lacking clarity.

clue.text: Where young players bring each other up

definitions.text: Where young players bring each other up

parts.words: Where young players bring each other up
parts.note: read as a playground plank on which two children take turns to lift each other into the air

explanation.surface: Sounds like a place where children raise one another, as in upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up' suggests rearing children, but here it is literal lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank pivoted in the middle, rising and falling as two children ride its ends.

clue.text: Budding engineers hacked by well-bred man

indicators.note: hacked means chopped about, so the letters for engineers are jumbled

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a gent is a gentleman, a man of good breeding

explanation.surface: Young engineers are cut down by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' rearranges REME into EMER, and 'by' simply joins it to GENT. REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Budding and emergent both describe something just beginning to appear or develop.

clue.text: Unrefined sailor's leader moves back to fifth place

indicators.text: leader moves back to fifth place
indicators.note: the first letter of the sailor word is shifted back so it sits fifth in line

parts.note: hearty is an old term for a sailor, as in 'me hearties'

explanation.surface: A crude seaman's captain is demoted to fifth place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' is the first letter of HEARTY, the H, which moves back to fifth place to leave EARTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down to earth, lacking polish.

clue.text: Barker's recovery guaranteeing us the game

definitions.text: Barker's recovery guaranteeing us the game

parts.words: Barker's recovery guaranteeing us the game
parts.note: read as a gun dog bringing back shot birds so the hunters keep their game

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sports team's comeback thanks to a player called Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the game' looks like a match being won, but it is shot birds fetched by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something, as a gundog fetches shot game.

clue.text: Horse of more than average height in Jerusalem

indicators.note: in places the height word inside the name for Jerusalem

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is a name for Jerusalem
tall means of above average height

explanation.surface: A tall horse seen in Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Scaly creature climbing over man

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in a down answer
in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the creature word is reversed

parts.note: an animal is a creature
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A scaly beast clambers over a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminated means made of thin layers or plates, like scales.

clue.text: One cannot go on for long in this way

definitions.text: One cannot go on for long in this way

parts.words: One cannot go on for long in this way
parts.note: read literally as a road closed at one end, so travel along it soon stops

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain lifestyle cannot be sustained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this way' sounds like a manner of living, but it is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street gives no through route.

clue.text: Like Christian, up in arms

definitions.meaning: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty in 1789
rebellious, ready to revolt against authority

explanation.definitionFit: Christian led the Bounty rising, and people up in arms are rebellious.

clue.text: It's playfully taken to be the name of a Finn

definitions.meaning: to take the ... is to tease playfully
a ... Finn is a drugged drink

explanation.definitionFit: The word is what one takes when teasing, and the first name in a doped-drink nickname.

clue.text: One deported before hijacking Russian plane

indicators.note: hijacking means seizing, so the word for before takes the plane inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone is expelled from a country before seizing a Soviet jet.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country, often forced out for political reasons.

clue.text: Level of command supplying English revolutionary with half our capital

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary

indicators.note: half takes the first three of the six letters

parts.note: London is the British capital, for a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A rank of officers is given to an English rebel along with part of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a rank or level in an organisation.

clue.text: Agree with officer serving porridge, say

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so serving it means being inside

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with an officer who is dishing out breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving porridge' looks like ladling oats but means doing time in jail. PORRIDGE is British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Two views that coincide agree or correspond exactly.

clue.text: Cry from bird shot crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the shot word goes either side of the river

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted shot in golf

explanation.surface: A bird cries out after being shot over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirp is a short high-pitched call of a small bird.

clue.text: Quickly grab a few notes

definitions.meaning: a short fragment of a song or tune

explanation.definitionFit: To seize swiftly is one sense; a brief fragment of music is the other.

clue.text: One dossing down in cargo boat?

definitions.meaning: a ... steamer carries cargo with no fixed route

explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant sleeping rough, and a freighter with no fixed schedule.

clue.text: Seat hitherto abandoned by the right

indicators.note: abandoned by means left without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: so far means hitherto, up to now
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A seat previously used by the political right has been given up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: End of ballade delivered in unbroken voices

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the words unbroken voices

explanation.surface: A poem's ending sung by boys whose voices have not yet broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'unbroken' and the start of 'voices'.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a ballade, addressing the reader or patron.

clue.text: Deficit Alice certainly didn't have

definitions.meaning: an amount by which something falls below what is needed
Alice in Wonderland tumbled a very long way down the rabbit hole, so her drop was anything but brief

explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount lacking; Alice's long tumble down the rabbit hole was the opposite of a brief drop.

clue.text: Very tidy, putting second tool with second container

parts.note: s again abbreviates second
a pick is a digging tool
and means together with
s again abbreviates second
a pan is a cooking container

explanation.surface: A neat arrangement of a tool stored next to a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Spick and span means spotlessly clean and neat.
